card_format: AI System Card + AI Risk Register (cybwaycard)

generator.name: cybwaycard
generator.mode: static analysis, offline, no model call, $0

intended_use: Asks the model what to run, then runs it.

checks.title: LLM usage inventoried
checks.guidance: Every model call site should be known and listed. Cybwaycard derives this from imports, API hosts and call names; keep model access behind one module so the inventory stays short.
checks.note: providers: OpenAI; call sites: 1; AI files: 1

checks.title: No hardcoded credentials
checks.guidance: Move keys to environment variables or a secret store; rotate any key that was committed. Values shown here are redacted at scan time.

checks.title: Credentials sourced from environment
checks.guidance: Read the key with os.environ / a secret manager and delete the literal.

checks.title: Code-enforced cost ceiling
checks.guidance: Add a budget object that is charged BEFORE each network call and raises when the ceiling would be exceeded. A dashboard alert is not a control; code is.

checks.title: Offline (mock) mode available
checks.guidance: Provide a deterministic mock provider (or dry-run) as the default so the suite runs at $0 and live calls are an explicit opt-in.

checks.title: Human approval gate, no auto-execute
checks.guidance: Model output reaches an execution primitive with no approval step in between. Route every consequential action through a logged approve/reject decision by a named human.

checks.title: Independent verification of model output
checks.guidance: Re-derive the claim from source data (a rule engine, a second independent check) and adjudicate PASS / REVIEW / QUARANTINE. The model must never grade its own output.

checks.title: Structured output validated
checks.guidance: Ask for strict JSON, parse it inside try/except, and validate the shape (schema, allowed values) before anything downstream reads it.

checks.title: Prompt-injection detection
checks.guidance: Scan untrusted input for published injection patterns before it reaches the prompt, plant a canary, and keep a red-team suite in the tests.

checks.title: Tamper-evident audit log
checks.guidance: Hash-chain the log (each entry carries the SHA-256 of the previous) and write a manifest of run outputs so edits, deletions and reordering are detectable.

checks.title: Accuracy evaluation exists
checks.guidance: Score the model against deterministic ground truth (precision / recall / F1 over N runs) and commit the numbers with the evidence that produced them.

checks.title: Drift / regression detection
checks.guidance: Diff each run against the previous one and fail CI when a previously passing case regresses. Model updates change behaviour silently.

checks.title: Model identifier declared
checks.guidance: Name the exact model in code (env-overridable), so a card and a benchmark can say which model produced which numbers.

checks.title: Explicit timeouts on model calls
checks.guidance: Pass an explicit timeout and a bounded retry count to the client; SDK defaults are generous and invisible in a review.

checks.title: Tests and CI present
checks.guidance: Governance claims need a test that fails when the control is removed, and a CI job that runs it on every push.

checks.title: CI runs without model API secrets
License and intended-use documentation
checks.guidance: State the license and, in the README's first paragraph, what the system is for and what it must not be used for. The card quotes that paragraph as the intended use.

checks.title: Dependencies pinned
checks.guidance: Pin every runtime dependency to an exact version (==) and bump deliberately; model SDKs change behaviour between minor versions.

checks.title: Data minimisation stated or enforced
checks.guidance: Write down exactly which fields reach the model (and which never do), and enforce it with a redaction / allow-list step in the prompt builder.

risk_register.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
risk_register.note: CARD-002 FAIL; CARD-003 FAIL; CARD-019 FAIL

risk_register.name: Data and Model Poisoning
risk_register.note: Training/fine-tuning data provenance is a runtime and supply-chain question, not visible in application code.

risk_register.name: System Prompt Leakage
risk_register.note: Whether a system prompt leaks depends on model behaviour at runtime; static analysis can only inventory prompts.

risk_register.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
risk_register.note: Requires review of the retrieval architecture and access controls on the vector store; not evaluable statically.

risk_register.name: Misinformation
risk_register.note: CARD-007 FAIL; CARD-011 FAIL; CARD-012 FAIL

risk_register.name: Unbounded Consumption
risk_register.note: CARD-004 FAIL; CARD-005 FAIL; CARD-014 FAIL

caveats: Static analysis only: the code was read, never executed. A control that exists in code may still be bypassed at runtime; a control implemented under an unusual name may be missed.
Checks are identifier and pattern heuristics with cited evidence. Treat a PASS as 'evidence found', not as certification, and a FAIL as 'no evidence found', not proof of absence.
Three OWASP LLM categories (LLM04, LLM07, LLM08) are reported as NOT ASSESSED because no honest static check exists for them.
Python sources only. Model calls made from other languages, notebooks, or shell scripts are not inventoried.
This card describes the application code around a model, not the model itself. Foundation-model training data, licences and safety evaluations belong to the model provider's own card.

references.owasp: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications — category names used with attribution to the OWASP Foundation
references.nist_ai_rmf: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1) — function/category identifiers; self-assessed mapping, not a conformance claim
